document.title: Make every durable report look and behave like the same product
document.summary: PRDs, designs, reports, decisions, research briefs, and diagram packets use one canonical report experience, explicit decision recording, and evidence-backed infrastructure-style SVG figures.
document.reviewFocus: Confirm that one rendering boundary and the globally approved Editorial Infrastructure language preserve domain-owned meaning while removing template and diagram ambiguity.
sources: Explicit user instruction on 2026-08-02: Apply Editorial Infrastructure globally.
Explicit user instruction on 2026-08-02: Replace the Excalidraw diagram style with a high-quality custom CSS/SVG diagram system inspired by Vercel's infrastructure diagrams.
Explicit user instruction on 2026-08-03: Use a white background with the square-grid effect across the entire page.

sections.title: Reviewers get one dependable document experience
sections.summary: The product is the review experience, not a collection of loosely synchronized templates.

items: Actor
A human reviewing an agent-generated durable document
Job and moment
Understand, discuss, and approve product or architecture truth in a browser
Capability
Read one consistent report, inspect a clean infrastructure explanation, and record real decisions
Entry
Open a generated PRD, design, report, decision, research, or diagram HTML artifact
Result
The reviewer can retell the outcome, reference stable anchors, and export decision input
Boundary
The report does not decide product truth, architecture, or approval on the reviewer's behalf

sections.title: Parallel templates made the review experience untrustworthy
sections.summary: Different report paths drifted in style, component availability, navigation, motion, decision state, and diagram generation.

blocks.text: Agents could select or imitate a PRD, design, generic report, or diagram shell rather than using one enforced report system. A generated document could therefore satisfy content instructions while visibly diverging from the expected template.

blocks.title: Review confidence breaks
blocks.text: A reviewer cannot know whether missing controls, inconsistent diagrams, or apparent decision state reflects product truth or generation drift.

items: Observed
A newly generated design did not follow the defined report template.
Repository evidence
Separate PRD, design, report, and diagram templates and CSS families existed.
Expected outcome
Every new durable artifact uses one recognizable shell and interaction contract.

sections.title: Meaning is composed first and rendered once
sections.summary: Domain skills decide required content; shared rendering and diagram skills provide consistent presentation.

items.title: Compose domain truth
items.text: PRD or Design Solution creates required sourced sections and decision lifecycle without authoring HTML.

items.title: Explain one system question
items.text: System Diagram produces an evidence-backed accessible infrastructure SVG.

items.title: Render one report
items.text: HTML Report Designer validates structured input and fills one canonical template.

items.title: Review and record
items.text: The human reads consistent navigation, records complete decision input, and exports Markdown.

items.title: Reconcile explicit approval
items.text: An agent updates canonical source only after the human explicitly approves the product or architecture choice.

items: New reports never select a document-specific shell or style family.
Every substantive PRD and durable design contains exactly one evidence-backed infrastructure-style System Diagram.
A decision cannot be recorded until option, rationale, and owner are present.
Browser-local state and exports never imply canonical approval.
Missing companion renderers block generation rather than trigger a lower-quality fallback.

sections.title: Review input becomes canonical truth only through explicit approval
sections.summary: The diagram separates report consistency, local recording, and human governance.

blocks.question: How does one consistent report carry a product or architecture decision from composition to explicit approval?
blocks.caption: Owning skills supply meaning, System Diagram supplies structured visual evidence, and the canonical report carries review input without self-approving it.
walkthrough: The reviewer asks for a PRD or design based on approved evidence.
The owning skill composes required meaning and gives System Diagram a bounded question.
One report presents that content and its decision controls consistently.
The reviewer records and exports complete review input.
Only explicit human approval updates canonical truth; incomplete input remains open.

sections.title: Three outcomes make the review system dependable

blocks.title: Render every durable document consistently
blocks.outcome: A reviewer sees one canonical shell, style, navigation, and component language regardless of document kind.
blocks.boundary: The renderer does not choose or reorder product and architecture content.

story.capability: open any durable agent-generated report in one consistent experience
story.outcome: format drift does not obscure the document's meaning

scenarios.title: Canonical generation
scenarios.given: an owning skill has complete validated structured content
scenarios.then: one portable report template produces self-contained HTML with actual-section navigation and stable review anchors

scenarios.title: Renderer unavailable
scenarios.given: the canonical renderer cannot be loaded
scenarios.when: the agent attempts final report generation
scenarios.then: generation blocks with a setup instruction instead of producing a substitute shell

steps.title: Supply meaning
steps.context: The owning skill has approved or clearly proposed content.
steps.response: The profile validator confirms required roles and lifecycle.
steps.outcome: The content is ready for canonical rendering.

steps.title: Open report
steps.action: The reviewer opens it in a browser.
steps.response: The same report shell, navigation, components, and fallbacks appear.
steps.outcome: The reviewer can focus on meaning rather than generation variance.

acceptance.text: Only one production report template and CSS source exist.
PRD, design, report, research, decision, and diagram kinds render through the same boundary.
Reports remain readable at 320px, without JavaScript, under reduced motion, and in print.

blocks.after: After this slice, reviewers recognize every durable document as the same report product.

blocks.title: Record decisions without implying approval
blocks.outcome: A reviewer can select, explain, record, restore, and export a real decision.
blocks.boundary: Recording does not mutate source or change document status to Approved.

story.capability: leave a complete portable decision record
story.outcome: an agent can reconcile the exact choice after explicit approval

scenarios.title: Complete review record
scenarios.given: a report contains an open or proposed decision
scenarios.when: the reviewer selects an option, provides rationale and owner, and checks Decision recorded
scenarios.then: the report persists and exports the stable decision record as review input

scenarios.title: Incomplete review record
scenarios.given: selection, rationale, or owner is missing
scenarios.when: the reviewer reaches the recording control
scenarios.then: the checkbox remains unavailable and identifies the missing work

steps.title: Choose and explain
steps.context: The decision shows concrete options and a custom path.
steps.action: The reviewer selects and adds rationale and owner.
steps.response: The record becomes eligible for completion.
steps.outcome: The choice is explicit and attributable.

steps.title: Record and export
steps.action: The reviewer checks Decision recorded and downloads Markdown.
steps.response: The report confirms local persistence and labels the export as review input.
steps.outcome: The exact stable ID can be reconciled after approval.

acceptance.text: Every decision renders a Decision recorded checkbox.
Recorded option, rationale, owner, date, and status survive reload and appear in export.
Accepted decisions require explicit approver/date in canonical source.

blocks.after: After this slice, reviewers can leave durable decision input without accidentally approving canonical truth.

blocks.title: Use one infrastructure visual language for every system diagram
blocks.outcome: PRD and design diagrams have one evidence, accessibility, visual, and regeneration contract.
blocks.boundary: The report renderer embeds figures but does not invent or redraw system semantics.

story.capability: follow one clear evidence-backed system path
story.outcome: the diagram teaches rather than decorating the report

scenarios.title: Consistent explanatory figure
scenarios.given: the owning skill names a diagram question and source-classified semantics
scenarios.then: the report shows searchable accessible infrastructure SVG with a clear primary route, explicit boundaries, semantic exceptions, and a text walkthrough

scenarios.title: Inconsistent visual language
scenarios.given: a figure uses hand-drawn or scene-local styling
scenarios.when: the canonical report attempts to include it
scenarios.then: generation rejects it instead of mixing diagram styles

steps.title: Define brief
steps.context: A substantive PRD or durable design requires one diagram.
steps.action: The owning skill supplies one question, boundary, and source-classified evidence.
steps.response: System Diagram receives one bounded brief instead of an open-ended drawing request.
steps.outcome: The semantic validation input is explicit.

steps.title: Validate semantics
steps.context: System Diagram has the bounded brief.
steps.action: It validates evidence, ownership, labels, route, accessibility text, and scene constraints.
steps.response: Invalid semantics stop; valid meaning becomes a deterministic system-diagram-v1 scene.
steps.outcome: A validated scene is handed to the renderer.

steps.title: Render and embed
steps.context: A validated system-diagram-v1 scene is available.
steps.action: System Diagram generates SVG and the report verifies provenance before embedding it.
steps.response: The report presents one accessible figure and its ordered walkthrough.
steps.outcome: The reviewer receives one legible explanatory figure.

acceptance.text: Every substantive PRD and durable design has exactly one consistent infrastructure-style System Diagram.
Hand-drawn or scene-local visual variants are rejected.
The same diagram remains understandable in desktop, narrow, no-JS, reduced-motion, and print review.

blocks.after: After this slice, every system diagram follows one teachable infrastructure visual language.

sections.title: One report and diagram system, without taking domain authority

items: In
Canonical schema, renderer, template, CSS, runtime, validators, decision recorder, System Diagram contract, and profile tests
Out
Automatic product/architecture decisions, source mutation from browser state, alternate diagram renderers, and implementation task creation
Legacy
Existing generated HTML remains readable but is not a valid source for new canonical output

blocks.question: How many production report templates should durable documents use?

options.label: One canonical report template and renderer
Separate templates for each document kind

blocks.rationale: One rendering boundary prevents drift while domain skills still own content roles.

blocks.question: Which visual language should every canonical report use?

options.label: Editorial Infrastructure across all canonical reports
Keep the previous compact documentation shell

blocks.rationale: Article-first hierarchy, one continuous white square-grid canvas, numbered chapters, ledger-style facts, inline decisions, and full-width infrastructure figures make dense product and architecture review easier to scan without splitting navigation and content into competing surfaces.

blocks.question: Which visual direction should system diagrams use?

options.label: Restrained infrastructure diagrams inspired by Vercel technical storytelling

blocks.rationale: A quiet grid, mostly white nodes, explicit boundaries, one blue causal route, and restrained semantic colors make technical explanations clearer and more authoritative.

blocks.question: How should reports capture real reviewer decisions?

options.label: Selection, rationale, owner, Decision recorded checkbox, persistence, and export

blocks.rationale: A structured portable record is clear to humans and agents while explicit approval remains separate.
